newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Chun's sentence cut from death to jail - state TV.
newsitem.headline: Chun's sentence cut from death to jail - state TV.

text.p: A South Korean Court on Monday reduced a death sentence handed down to former president Chun Doo Hwan to life in jail, and cut to 17 years from 22-1/2 years the jail term for another ex-president Roh Tae-woo, state television reported.

Chun was sentenced to death in August for mutiny, treason and bribery over a 1979 coup, a massacre in 1980 in the city of Kwangju that crushed democratic opposition and for amassing a slush fund worth hundreds of millions of dollars.
Roh was convicted on similar charges involving the same incidents.

A three-judge panel said Chun's death sentence was commuted because of his contribution to economic development and the peaceful transfer of the presidency to Roh in 1988, the Korea Broadcasting System said.
Chun was fined 263 billion won ($311.6 million) and Roh 226 billion won. (Conversion: $1 = 844 won)
